summary: Built the four declared outputs of M3-S04 — discountApprovalPanel.html, .js, .js-meta.xml and __tests__/discountApprovalPanel.test.js — and nothing else; no .css was written because the plan declares none and an undeclared file in the artefact tree is one check-outputs never confirms. The panel reads Discount__c and Approval_Status__c through the platform twice over and through Apex not at all: lightning-record-view-form renders them with the platform's labels, Percent formatting and per-field FLS, while @wire(getRecord) provisions the same two fields so the button rule can be computed in JavaScript. Both go through Lightning Data Service and share its cache. The Submit button calls OpportunityApprovalController.submitForApproval(Id opportunityId) — the @AuraEnabled entry point M3-S03 built, never the @InvocableMethod, which cannot carry @AuraEnabled — and handles both refusal shapes: a returned SubmitOutcome with success=false and a message (Q30's shape, and the ordinary case) and a thrown error (the exceptional one). Success refreshes the record with notifyRecordUpdateAvailable([{recordId}]), which is Q34's 'the component refreshes the record after submit' and the documented call for a UI API wire; refreshApex on a non-Apex adapter is deprecated and is not used. The threshold is the discountThreshold design attribute defaulting to 20, coerced with Number() because App Builder hands Integer properties over as strings. The declared checker exits 0 with the exact line the plan's test description predicted, and was proven live against two deliberately broken scratch copies rather than trusted on a zero-finding line. check-outputs ok; the one XML file parses. The Jest suite was NOT run: @salesforce/sfdx-lwc-jest is not installed, this repo has no package.json or node_modules, and installing one is forbidden by the agent's Scope Guardrails. No compile check was possible and nothing was deployed.
confidence_rationale: AGENT_CONTRACT.md Gate C row 3 caps confidence at MEDIUM when no compile check ran, and none could: no org alias was supplied, so there was no way to validate the bundle against an org. Two further unexecuted checks push in the same direction rather than lower: the Jest suite could not be run for want of a harness, and no JavaScript parse check ran either — `node --check` exits 0 on deliberately broken input once a file contains an `import` statement (proven here with a control file), and V8 does not parse the decorators an LWC module uses, so there is no stdlib-adjacent parser in this environment that would catch a syntax error in the .js. Everything else meets the HIGH bar: every mandatory input came from plan.json, every import resolves to a file under the build (the Apex method by exact signature and parameter name, both fields by path), every lightning-* tag and attribute is quoted from a cited skill's code-examples with the source's own UNVERIFIED markers carried across, and the one declared checker exits 0 with its liveness proven in both directions. The single inline UNVERIFIED marker is assumption A35's Percent reading, which the plan already carries as a medium-risk assumption, not an unresolved symbol.

dimensions_skipped.reason: The bundle dispatches exactly one event — ShowToastEvent, whose bubbles/composed shape is the platform module's, not this component's. It has no parent to notify and no sibling to coordinate with (M3-S05 drops it into a sidebar region on its own), so there is no CustomEvent of its own to shape. Emitting one for symmetry would be an unread public surface.

Sixteen Jest cases were written, including the four the step's manual acceptance test names verbatim, and the cited jest-a11y checker's assertion rules pass over them. None of them was executed: @salesforce/sfdx-lwc-jest does not resolve in this environment (proven), there is no package.json or jest.config.js, and the agent's Scope Guardrails forbid npm install. The suite is reviewed evidence, not passing evidence.

findings.title: `next`'s --add-checker advice would block this step on two of its three suggestions
findings.detail: build_plan.py next advises declaring check_wire_service_patterns.py, check_lwc_jest_testing_with_accessibility.py and check_invocable_methods.py on M3-S04, and § 5's validate WARN says the same. All three were run here as supplementary evidence, and only one of the three would be a real assertion. check_wire_service_patterns.py --manifest-dir artefacts/M3-S04 exits 0 with 0 findings over 1 JavaScript file and is worth declaring. check_lwc_jest_testing_with_accessibility.py --root artefacts/M3-S04 --project-root . exits 1 with exactly two findings, both of which are 'package.json not found at project root' and 'jest.config.js not found at project root' — the build directory is not an SFDX project and this step declares neither file, so declaring this checker would fail a correct step for the absence of files no step in this plan produces. Its four rules that do bear on the bundle (a __tests__ directory exists, the test file carries a11y assertions, no document.querySelector, no setTimeout) all pass. check_invocable_methods.py --manifest-dir artefacts/M3-S04 prints 'WARN: no Apex classes found' and exits 0 with score 100 — it would assert nothing, because the invocable lives in M3-S03. The skill is cited here for knowledge (why the LWC imports the controller and not the action), which is a legitimate read with no artefact of this step to check.

findings.recommendation: Declare only check_wire_service_patterns.py, with amend-step --add-checker lwc/wire-service-patterns, while the step is still amendable. Leave the other two WARNs standing and say why: one asserts about a project layout the build layer does not have, the other about Apex this step does not ship. Library follow-up: check_lwc_jest_testing_with_accessibility.py's two project-setup rules are the only thing separating it from a build-layer-usable checker; a --skip-project-setup flag, or demoting those two to advisory, would make it declarable on any build step.

findings.title: `node --check` is a silent no-op on any file containing an import statement, so it reads as a passing syntax check while asserting nothing
findings.detail: The obvious way to sanity-check an emitted .js without a harness is `node --check <file>`. It exits 0 on this bundle's JavaScript — and it also exits 0 on a control file containing `import { x } from "y";` followed by unbalanced braces. The same node build fails correctly (exit 1, SyntaxError printed) on a broken CommonJS file with no import statement, so the failure mode is specific: once module detection kicks in, --check stops reporting. Separately, V8 does not parse the decorator syntax (@api, @wire) an LWC module uses at all, so even a working ESM --check would be the wrong parser. Reported because a future run in this build could quite reasonably quote a green `node --check` as evidence the file compiles, exactly as this run nearly did.

evidence.control_broken_esm: import { x } from "y"; class A { @api foo; bar( { }  -> node --check exit 0
evidence.control_broken_cjs: function f( {  -> node --check exit 1, SyntaxError: Unexpected end of input

findings.recommendation: Do not quote `node --check` as evidence for an LWC .js file. There is no parser in this environment that handles decorators; the real check is the Jest run (which needs the sfdx-lwc-jest harness) or an org-side dry run via scripts/mock_deploy.py, both of which are the human's.

findings.title: The component's user-facing strings are hard-coded English, because this build ships no CustomLabel
findings.detail: skills/lwc/lwc-internationalization and agents/lwc-builder/AGENT.md Step 3 both say user-facing text belongs in custom labels imported through @salesforce/label, so the bundle is not pinned to en-US. Every sentence in this panel — the button label, the six-branch hint, the outcome messages and the toast titles — is a literal instead. The reason is structural rather than an oversight: no step in this plan produces a CustomLabel artefact, so a @salesforce/label import would resolve to nothing at deploy time, and adding one would be an output this step does not declare (§ 4, borrowed-agent condition 2).

evidence.query: string literals in submitHint, handleSubmit and failWith

findings.recommendation: If Northwind ever runs this org in more than one language, the remedy is a CustomLabel step ahead of M3-S04 and a re-run of this one; it is not a change this step could have made on its own. Worth a line in the M3 milestone report so the gate sees it.

process_observations.observation: The upstream artefacts were precise enough to build against without a single guess: the controller's method signature and parameter name, the picklist's exact three values and the fact that blank means nothing was ever submitted all came off files in this build rather than from memory.

The plan's step note had already settled the data strategy, the refresh call, the toast module and the design-attribute threshold against the rule each one follows, and every one of those held on contact with the skills; the note predicted the checker's output line word for word and the run reproduced it.

The validation rule written in M2-S03 already tells the rep to 'submit for approval from the Discount panel', so the error message a blocked save produces and the panel this step builds name each other — coherence across two milestones that nothing in the plan forced.

Two of the three checkers next advises declaring on this step cannot assert anything about it — one fails on the absence of a package.json the build layer never has, the other finds no Apex because the Apex is in M3-S03 — so following the printed advice verbatim would block a correct step.
